clue.text: Profile of Charlie taking trip overseas perhaps

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a band or team taking a trip abroad is on tour

explanation.surface: A travel writer's profile of a man called Charlie heading abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is an outline, the shape traced by the edge of something, as a profile is.

clue.text: Reason to accept large part of sentence

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: a cause is a reason for something

explanation.surface: A judge has reason to accept a long prison term.
explanation.definitionFit: A clause is a grammatical unit, a section of a sentence with its own verb.

clue.text: Tight times could be close

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy, tight with money
by is the multiplication sign read aloud, as in three by four

explanation.surface: Times of financial hardship could be approaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby means not far away, in the vicinity.

clue.text: Too much of article included in open work

indicators.note: included in means the article sits within the pair of words

parts.note: overt means open, not concealed
the is the definite article
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A grammar point about an article in an open-ended work.
explanation.definitionFit: Over-the-top means excessive, exaggerated beyond what is reasonable.

clue.text: Fasten stand with top missing

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a trivet is a stand for a hot pot or kettle

explanation.surface: Bolt down a stand that has lost its top.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to join metal plates firmly with a metal pin.

clue.text: Quick inspection from king in lavatory, lots of water reported

parts.note: loo is an informal British word for a lavatory

indicators.note: reported means we want the word that is heard, not the one that is written

parts.note: the sea is a large body of water

explanation.surface: A monarch's flooded toilet gets a hurried glance.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOK-SEE is informal British slang for a brief look.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is a casual, brief glance over something, a quick survey.

clue.text: Regularly jumpy after match in Paris? Relax!

indicators.note: after means the jumpy letters follow the match and the French word

parts.note: a match gives a light
en is French for in
alternate letters of jumpy

explanation.surface: Someone nervous after a match in France is told to calm down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighten up is an informal command to stop being so serious or tense.

clue.text: Just nothing on lake in New York

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

indicators.note: in means lake's letter goes within New York's

explanation.surface: Simply nothing on a lake in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Only and just both mean merely, no more than.

clue.text: Cooler overhead

parts.note: something above your head that keeps you cool, not a fridge or a running cost

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' suggests a drinks box and 'overhead' a business cost; it is a parasol or awning.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade shields people from the heat of the sun from above.

clue.text: Eternally growing

definitions.meaning: first meaning: forever, for all time
second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer means more and more.
explanation.definitionFit: Evermore means always, for all future time; ever more describes something steadily increasing.

clue.text: Open-mouthed, commander exercises

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander or chief
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: An officer gapes in astonishment at the drills.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape describes someone staring with the jaw dropped in wonder or surprise.

clue.text: Unofficial enforcer leaving it in a mess

indicators.note: letters in a mess are jumbled up, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A self-appointed lawman walks away and leaves things chaotic.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigilante is a citizen who punishes wrongdoers without legal authority.

clue.text: Replace vessel, having found all but the first two?

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel

indicators.note: keep every letter of the word except the opening pair

parts.note: to found an organisation is to institute it

explanation.surface: Someone replaces a ship after discovering only part of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' looks like the past tense of find, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: To substitute something is to put it in place of another, a swap.

clue.text: Lady married son of Arkwright!

parts.note: a lady is a she, a female person

explanation.surface: A woman wed a son of Arkwright, the mill-owning family name.
explanation.walkthrough: The ark-wright is Noah, builder of the ark; the exclamation mark flags the joke. Arkwright looks like a surname.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Shem is one of Noah's three sons, alongside Ham and Japheth.

clue.text: Happen to arrive at mountain route

parts.note: to come to a place is to arrive at it
a pass is a route through mountains

explanation.surface: Hikers will eventually reach the mountain crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Come to pass is a formal, biblical phrase meaning occur or take place.

clue.text: Hierarchical structure of people kissing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ranking of status within a group
second meaning, playful: an order (a society) of people who peck, give quick kisses

explanation.walkthrough: A peck is a quick kiss, so the question mark treats the phrase as a fraternity of kissers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from hens establishing rank by pecking, now used for any social hierarchy.

clue.text: Repaired broken set, it's found by the way

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, so the letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A broken set was mended, and it turned up incidentally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the way' looks like 'incidentally' but means beside the road; a kerb is the edge of a pavement.
explanation.definitionFit: Kerbstones line the edge of the roadway, separating the pavement from traffic.

clue.text: Crops Dai scattered occasionally at intervals

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, as in 'the gunfire was occasionally at intervals'

indicators.note: scattered letters are spread about and land in a new order

explanation.surface: A Welshman called Dai sows his crops here and there.
explanation.definitionFit: Sporadic describes things happening irregularly, now and then, not continuously.

clue.text: No profit in fuel that's enormous

indicators.note: in means one word goes within the other

parts.note: coal is a fuel
a loss is the opposite of a profit

explanation.surface: A fuel business making no money is a huge problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Colossal means gigantic, like the Colossus of Rhodes.

clue.text: Quietly angry with a gopher, somehow Schofield finally snapped

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
hot under the collar means angry

indicators.note: somehow says these letters reach the answer in some other order
finally takes the last letter of Schofield

parts.note: last letter of Schofield

explanation.surface: TV presenter Phillip Schofield finally loses his temper with a gopher and is caught on camera.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap someone is to take a quick photograph of them.

clue.text: Hammer crude metal left inside

indicators.note: inside means left's letter goes within the jumbled word
crude metal is unrefined, so the letters are in raw disorder

explanation.surface: A hammer made of rough metal is left within.
explanation.definitionFit: A mallet is a hammer with a large wooden or rubber head.

clue.text: Embarrass when performance finished

parts.note: a show is a performance
up means finished, as in time's up

explanation.surface: An actor is embarrassed when the play is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To show someone up is to humiliate them by exposing their faults.

clue.text: Underground feature that may be square?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the part of a plant below the soil
second meaning: in maths a ... may be a square ...

explanation.walkthrough: 'Underground' suggests the London Tube, but it is just below ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants anchor themselves in soil by roots, and arithmetic has square and cube roots.

clue.text: Film course for unstable person

parts.note: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 thriller
a path is a course or route

explanation.surface: A film studies course might cover a disturbed character.
explanation.definitionFit: A psychopath is a person with a severe personality disorder, mentally unbalanced and often dangerous.

clue.text: About to plunder chocolate 11

definitions.note: 11 is SUBSTITUTE, so this reads chocolate substitute

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
to rob is to plunder

explanation.surface: Someone about to steal chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Carob powder, from the pods of a Mediterranean tree, is used as a chocolate substitute.

clue.text: Low river seen in high ground

parts.note: to low is to moo, the sound cattle make

explanation.surface: A low-lying river visible on the uplands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like the opposite of high, but it is the verb for a cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: A moor is open upland, high uncultivated ground covered in heather.

clue.text: Bring shame on Diane's integrity

parts.note: Di is short for Diane, and the possessive adds the s
honour means integrity, moral uprightness

explanation.surface: A woman's good name is disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: To dishonour someone is to disgrace them, damaging their reputation.

clue.text: In mag, Lowestoft is gleaming

indicators.note: In says the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of mag and the start of Lowestoft

explanation.surface: A magazine feature says the Suffolk coastal town Lowestoft is shining.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglow means glowing with light or colour, radiant and bright.

clue.text: Heat unit Claire rebuilt with nothing inside

indicators.note: inside means the zero goes within the rearranged name
a name rebuilt has its letters put together in a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Claire's heating system is rebuilt with nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A calorie is a measure of heat energy, used for food energy.

clue.text: Stage from which one might be transported

definitions.text: Stage from which one might be transported

parts.words: Stage from which one might be transported
parts.note: a stage is a fare stage on a bus route, and being transported means carried away, not enraptured as the theatre suggests

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stage' and 'transported' suggest a theatre audience carried away with delight; it is a place passengers board.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers wait at a bus stop to be carried on to their destination.
